lead.headline: Verstappen wins at Sepang, his first victory of the season, after a 90-minute delay
lead.byline: FORMULA 1 · AL JAZEERA · SKY SPORTS · 4 OCT
lead.short: From pole, Verstappen beat the championship leader Kimi Antonelli, with Lewis Hamilton third after falling to 18th when a Ferrari tyre gamble went wrong. The start was pushed back twice, by rain and by software failures that stopped several Ferrari-powered cars, and the 55 laps were interrupted twice by the safety car. George Russell retired late on.
more: It is Verstappen's first win of 2026; Mercedes had won the three races before. The next race is in Singapore on Sunday.

why.text: The win Max had been waiting for all year, on the day the weather and the software did their best to stop it.

update.front: Max's first win of the season is the day's news for this reader on its own.

seconds.headline: Supreme Court declines to suspend the Chief Election Commissioner but issues notice to the Centre and the Commission
seconds.byline: HINDUSTAN TIMES · TIMES OF INDIA · 5 OCT
seconds.short: The court said it could not pass an order against Gyanesh Kumar on the strength of news reports, but asked the government and the Election Commission to respond to the plea, and said it wanted to see who modified Form 6. Protests against him continued for a third day.

why.text: The first time the court has put the Commission's own conduct on its docket; the replies will be the first official account.

update.new: The Supreme Court heard the plea: no suspension, but notice to the Centre and the Commission.
update.front: The Supreme Court's first order on the Chief Election Commissioner is front-page news on its own.

facts.sc: no suspension; notice to Centre and ECI
facts.form6: court wants to know who modified it

seconds.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro tops Brazil's first round with 47%; he faces Lula in a runoff on 25 October
seconds.byline: NPR · AGÊNCIA BRASIL · WASHINGTON POST · 4 OCT
seconds.short: The senator, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, took 47.03% of valid votes to Lula's 45.16%, beating the polls, which had Lula ahead. Neither passed 50%, so they meet again in three weeks. Abstention, at 21%, was the highest in a first round since 1998.

why.text: Brazil is India's partner in BRICS; a change of government in Brasília would reshape that relationship.

seconds.headline: Claude can now run on servers in India through Amazon Bedrock
seconds.short: Requests sent to the India endpoint are processed in the country, which lets banks, insurers and public bodies with data-residency rules use Claude Opus 5, Sonnet 5 and Haiku 4.5. Reliance and CRED tested it in a private preview.

why.text: The biggest barrier for Indian banks and insurers using these models was where the data goes; this removes it.

monday.mood: The Sensex opened 453 points higher after eight straight losing weeks, helped by firmer Asian markets, easier oil and fading bets on a US rate rise after weak American jobs data. Most of the gain had gone by 13:00, with HDFC Bank down about 2%; IT and pharma lagged.
weekend: Weak US jobs figures on Friday (29,000 added) cut the odds of a US rate rise, which had been pulling money out of Indian shares.
Crude flows through Hormuz rose above pre-war levels, easing oil prices despite the Houthi claim of a strike on Aramco in Riyadh.
Flávio Bolsonaro led Brazil's first round, sending the election to a runoff with Lula on 25 October.
IndiGo raised its fuel charge, and companies began posting second-quarter business updates.

notes.Sensex: Opened higher after eight losing weeks, then gave most of it back by early afternoon.
notes.Nifty 50: Back above 22,500 at the open on better global cues, then pared.
notes.Nifty Bank: HDFC Bank fell about 2% after its quarterly business update.
notes.Nifty IT: Lagged before TCS's results on Wednesday.
notes.S&P 500: Rose on Friday as weak hiring lifted hopes the Fed will hold.
notes.Brent crude: Eased as crude flows through Hormuz rose above pre-war levels.
notes.USD/INR: Near its weakest since late July, with the euro at a 17-month low against the dollar.
notes.Gold 24K: Held back by a firm dollar.
